title: Dynamic Target Leeway Autoscaler — composite-target algorithms and hard safety fences for Dedicated fleets
creator: Miguel Torres
description: Problem: Dedicated fleets need autoscaling policies that meet per-tenant throughput SLAs while minimizing cost and avoiding dangerous oscillations. Current controllers either react to a single metric (latency or GPU utilization) or apply aggressive surge rules that cause expensive overprovisioning and occasional instability during bursts. We need a policy engine that composes multiple target metrics, exposes tunable leeway (headroom) parameters, and enforces hard safety fences (rate limits, max surge, cooldowns) for Dedicated capacity.
context: Customers purchase Dedicated pools with committed throughput guarantees. We must honor both steady-state commitments and bounded burst behavior without exposing noisy scaling behavior to tenant apps.

Existing autoscalers in the repo are mostly reactive single-metric controllers (CPU/GPU util) or fixed-threshold scalers. This ticket proposes a composable policy engine adjustable per-pooled-fleet and per-tenant override.

Key trade-offs: aggressive scaling reduces SLO breaches but increases cost; conservative scaling saves cost but risks tail latency and failed requests. Safety fences must prioritize reliability and predictable billing.
This design ties into routing (fallback to hosted), billing (headroom credits), and Console (dashboards and per-route targets).
goals: Design and spec a composite-target autoscaling engine that combines throughput, p95 latency, queue depth, and GPU token/sec into a single scaling target with tunable weights.
Introduce a 'leeway' / headroom abstraction that translates SLA slack into actionable capacity reservations and transient burst credits.
Define deterministic safety limits: max scale-up rate, max surge fraction, minimum cool-down windows, and cost budget pluggable policies.
Provide a rollout plan (canary + simulation) and telemetry/metrics required to validate behavior under synthetic and production workloads.
Ship runtime config (YAML) schema and SDK flags for Dedicated control plane to expose per-fleet policy knobs.

proposal: Composite target formula: target_instances = ceil( max( weighted_throughput_target, latency_backoff_target, queue_depth_target, utilization_target ) ) with configurable weights and smoothing windows.
Throughput target: compute desired instances from 95th-percentile observed tokens/sec per-instance baseline with a short window (30s).
Latency backoff target: translate p95 latency > target into multiplicative headroom until latency returns below threshold for N consecutive windows.
Queue depth target: linear allocation based on queued requests per instance; soft cap triggers vertical bump for small bursts.
Utilization target: low-weight component to prevent overfitting to transient latency spikes (uses EWMA of GPU utilization).

Leeway / headroom credit subsystem: each fleet has a committed baseline, an allocated headroom fraction, and a replenishing burst-credit pool. Credit consumption is meterable and charged to the tenant's burst budget when applicable.
Safety fences (hard limits):
- max_scale_up_rate: cap on number of instances added per minute (default: +20% of current fleet or +8 instances, whichever smaller).
- max_surge_fraction: total instances cannot exceed committed_capacity * (1 + surge_fraction) (default surge_fraction 0.35).
- cooldown_window: minimum time between scale events affecting the same instance group (default 90s).
- step_limit: maximum single scaling step (default 4 instances).
- rollback_triggers: persistent error rate > 3% or API error spike correlated with scale-up triggers automatic rollback to last known stable config and alert.
- cost_guard: if projected hourly billing delta exceeds configured budget cap, treat additional scale as 'deferred' unless explicit override by SRE or customer.
Hysteresis and smoothing: use leaky-integrator on target delta with separate tau for scale-up and scale-down to bias toward safer downward moves being slower (scale-down tau longer).
Priority and fairness: for multi-tenant pools, apply priority weights and preemptible credits; low-priority tenants can be curtailed when global safeguards trigger.
Observability: expose the computed target, contributing metric components (with weights), credit balances, and safety-fence activations as time-series and Console panels.

Config schema: fleet_policy.yaml with fields: weights (throughput, latency, queue, util), leeway_percent, surge_fraction, max_scale_up_rate, cooldown_window, step_limit, priority_class, cost_budget_id.
API: control plane endpoints to get/set policy, retrieve simulated scale decisions for a given metric history window, and run dry-run mode for planned rollouts.
Testing: offline simulation harness using historical telemetry; stress tests on a staging fleet with injected latencies and load patterns; chaos tests to validate rollback triggers.
Rollout: feature-flag gated; start with 10% of fleets (internal staging -> pilot customers) then ramp to all Dedicated fleets. Canary monitored via synthetic SLO tests and cost delta dashboards.
Docs and Console: clear UX for setting per-fleet leeway and cost caps, plus real-time dashboards showing headroom consumption and predicted scale events.
Backwards compatibility: if a fleet has legacy static autoscaler config, use migration tooling to translate thresholds to an equivalent composite policy with conservative defaults.
Implementation owners: infra-autoscaling team (primary), runtime-team (kernel scheduling hooks), console (dashboards & policy editor), billing-infra (cost guard integration).
Estimated engineering work: design + implementation + validation -> 3 sprints across owners (13 points estimate).
acceptance_criteria: Specs: A completed design doc with formulas and schema checked in to /internal/docs/dedicated-autoscale/dynamic-leeway.md.
Runtime: Ability to apply a fleet_policy.yaml to a Dedicated fleet and observe the 'computed_target' metric emitted every 30s.
Safety: Default safety fences enforced on staging fleet: max_scale_up_rate, max_surge_fraction, cooldown_window, and rollback triggers all functional under test scenarios.
Telemetry: Console shows breakdown of composite target contributors and a live headroom credit gauge; alerts fire when cost_guard would block scaling.
Simulations: Offline simulator reproduces expected scale decisions for at least three recorded burst patterns (short spike, long ramp, plateau-with-noise).
Rollout: Feature flag gated canary deployed to single internal pilot fleet with monitoring runbook and incident escalation documented.
Docs: Console settings and API reference for fleet_policy.yaml published and linked in the PR description.
Signal: No increase in production SLO violations attributable to the new autoscaler during canary window (target: <=1 incident related to scaling decisions).

comments: 2026-02-12 Miguel Torres: Added initial proposal; leaning toward multiplicative latency backoff rather than additive to better handle heavy-tailed tails.
2026-02-16 Asha Patel: Reviewed weights proposal — suggested default weights: throughput=0.6, latency=0.25, queue=0.1, util=0.05. Added note to make weights editable per-fleet.
2026-02-20 Priya Rao (Product): Need to include cost guard concept tied to customer burst billing. Product requests per-tenant opt-out if under enterprise contract.
2026-02-25 SRE: Concerned about surge_fraction default of 0.35; proposed lowering to 0.25 for initial canary, with explicit ramping.
2026-03-03 Billing infra: Headroom credits require a new metering label; PR with schema draft linked above.
notes: Decision: use asymmetric smoothing (faster scale-up, slower scale-down) to avoid oscillation under noisy load.
Decision: default surge_fraction for canary set to 0.25; final value configurable per-contract.
Follow-up: define SLO-exempt tenants for whom scaling can be disabled (eg. low-priority preemptible workloads).
